| [`line-recoil-in-crystal`](ledger-core-coherent-physics.md#line-recoil-in-crystal) | research claim (#527). Inside a kinematic crystal slab, the zero-phonon PXR/CBS line centre is the exact vacuum root of `line-recoil-resonance`. The lattice takes `+hbar*g` without energy; initial and final free-like Bloch branches obey the vacuum mass shell up to the common mean inner potential and Bloch branch shifts. A finite slab broadens the line around that centre. At 10–15 keV graphite/hBN (002)/(004) geometries, the omitted in-medium corrections move the harmonic defect `2E2 - E4` by ≤ 0.6 eV. The components are: mean inner potential (cancels in the defect, linear in `g`; single lines +0.3 to +0.7 eV); photon refraction with exit-face tangential continuity (`k_eff = omega (n + delta h)`, +0.25 to +0.58 eV on the defect over the 13 rows and both detector-azimuth conventions, ≤ 0.3 eV per line at the sized geometries); and entrance refraction (< 0.001 eV). Two-beam Bloch branch shifts of the free-like branch depend on the unreported in-plane crystal azimuth (median ≈ 0.4–0.5 eV on the defect, up to several eV near a strong Bragg condition). The excitation-weighted branch centroid is unshifted at two-beam order, so at EDS resolution they broaden rather than move the line. The straight-path exact root reproduces Huang et al.'s measured defect, `18.19 ± 0.66` eV measured against `19.10` eV predicted (19.5 eV with exit-face photon refraction, −2.0σ). The straight classical root gives `0` and is excluded at 27σ (≥ 11σ if the ±0.5 eV calibration error is uncorrelated between the two lines). Huang's own scattering Monte Carlo predicts ≈ 15.7 eV (quantum) and ≈ −2.5 eV (classical) for Fig. 1d, so the straight-path agreement does not test their transport/peak-fit bias. Not claimed: many-beam dynamical diffraction, electron Bragg-resonant geometries, phonon-assisted lines, absolute line energies (Huang's tilts were fitted with their quantum model), peak-fit bias from multiple scattering, the unreported detector azimuth (`phi_obs` = 0 pinned; 180° gives a 18.04 eV prediction), any production kernel change. | `anchored` |

That is forward incoherent bremsstrahlung emitted along `Q̂ = (k n + g)/\|k n + g\|`, Bragg-diffracted into `n` at `E_B = −ħc g²/(2 n·g)`. By reciprocity a row emitting the unattenuated brem density `j(Q̂, E)` at depth `z` contributes `j(Q̂, E)·½Σ_s\|D_s(L − z, E)\|²` per steradian of `n`. `D_s(u) = b[e^{iλ_1u} − e^{iλ_2u}]/(λ_1 − λ_2)` is the diffracted amplitude of the time-reversed two-beam Laue mode (unit transmitted, zero diffracted at the exit face), and `λ_1,2` are the eigenvalues of `N = [[kχ_0/2n_s, a],[b, q + k²χ_0/2Q_s]]`, with `q = −det/2Q_s`, `det = g² + 2k n·g`, `ab = k⁴\|χ_g\|²C_s²/(4k n_sQ_s)` and `\|b\|² = k⁴\|χ_g\|²C_s²/(4Q_s²)`. Kinematically, `∫dE\|D\|² = \|b\|²2πu ħcQ_s/\|n·g\|`, linear in the remaining depth `u`. `j` is the native track-length brem density (same continuum model, tables, cutoff and channeling flux weight) toward `Q̂` at `E_B`, without the escape factor; the mode carries both beams' absorption (`Im χ_0`), refraction (`Re χ_0`) and Pendellösung depletion (`ab`). | `rederived` |
| [`diffracted-characteristic-radiation`](ledger-core-coherent-physics.md#diffracted-characteristic-radiation) | every perfect single-slab crystal case adds to `spec_characteristic` the signed Kossel term of each characteristic line near a Laue Bragg energy `E_B = −ħc g²/(2 n·g)` toward `n`. The term is `S(E) = Y 𝓛(E) Σ_k w_k [½Σ_s(\|T_s\|² + \|D_s\|²) − \|T_0\|² + Re(φ_Z X)](L − z_k, E)`, with `X = ½Σ_s 2C_s T_s* D_s`. | `anchored` |
| [`node-support-window-tail`](ledger-core-coherent-physics.md#node-support-window-tail) | support-windowed incoherent node scoring adds a cycle-averaged endpoint-cluster expansion through inverse fourth power, with exact near-window corrections. Affine dispersion uses the effective slope, pole and residue exactly; general dispersion uses a frozen-denominator surrogate fenced by `rho <= 1/x_c < 1`. Cluster membership bounds full-band phase drift against one representative; the multipole ratio is at most 0.1. An aggregate weak-field envelope (including higher moments and remainder) and an all-dispersion-interval beat-gap fence control window widening. These are absolute field/envelope statements, not a universal relative spectral-error guarantee; numerical margins require qualification. | `rederived` |
